Best t-SNE Result From Multiple Initializations

Source: R/iterated.R
smallvis_rep.Rd

Run t-SNE multiple times from a random initialization, and return the embedding with the lowest cost.

Usage

smallvis_rep(nrep = 10, keep_all = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

nrep

Number of repeats.

keep_all

If TRUE, then the return value is a list of lists, indexed from 1 .. nrep, with each entry the result from each smallvis run. Otherwise just the result with the lowest error is returned.

...

Arguments to apply to each smallvis run.

Value

The smallvis result with the lowest final cost, or if keep_all is TRUE all results as a list, indexed as 1 .. nrep. If ret_extra is not FALSE, then the final costs for all nrep runs are also included in the return value list as a vector called all_costs. In this case, if keep_all is TRUE, then all_costs appears as an extra item on all results. Additionally, each result will have an extra entry best_rep, giving the index of the result with the lowest cost.

Details

This function ignores any value of Y_init you set, and uses Y_init = "rand".

Built-in methods prepare input scaling, PCA, and affinities once. All starts share that input graph, including when using approximate neighbors, and each start resets its coordinates and optimizer state. Custom constructors prepare their input separately for each run. Runs are ranked by the sum of costs at their returned coordinates, independently of epoch history. Per-run time_secs excludes the shared input preparation.

Examples

set.seed(42)
best <- smallvis_rep(
  nrep = 2, X = iris, perplexity = 30, max_iter = 100,
  ret_extra = TRUE, epoch_callback = FALSE, n_threads = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)
range(best$all_costs)
#> [1] 0.1421794 0.2018069

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Return best result out of five random initializations
tsne_iris_best <- smallvis_rep(
  nrep = 5, X = iris, perplexity = 50, method = "tsne",
  ret_extra = TRUE
)
# How much do the costs vary between runs?
range(tsne_iris_best$all_costs)
# Display best embedding found
plot(tsne_iris_best$Y)

# Keep all results
# First result is in tsne_iris_rep[[1]], second in tsne_iris_rep[[2]] etc.
tsne_iris_rep <- smallvis_rep(
  nrep = 5, X = iris, perplexity = 50, method = "tsne",
  ret_extra = TRUE, keep_all = TRUE
)
# Index of result with smallest error is in special list item 'best_rep'
best_iris <- tsne_iris_rep[[tsne_iris_rep[[1]]$best_rep]]
} # }
